top_choice_rationale: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new regime of correlated matter: the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of vanishing Dirac velocity was tested sharply by the 2018 discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states at the predicted angle, and the phenomenology has been reproduced by many independent groups and carried to other moire platforms. The citation is kept to prediction plus discovery of the phases and claims nothing about pairing mechanism. The remaining weaknesses (Andrei's precursor STM work, omitted 2018 first authors, device dependence) are real but are scope and attribution issues that a narrow citation handles. Optical lattice clocks (P002) are well reproduced across laboratories but are a refinement of precision metrology after the 2005 and 2012 prizes, so I rank them second, above no award.
recusal_note: Possible but weak: as WACQT director at Chalmers I work close to superconducting-circuit groups, but none of the proposed laureates (twisted graphene, optical lattice clocks) is a Chalmers or WACQT colleague or collaborator, so no recusal apparent from profile.
